hints.title: Index Simulation Pattern
hints.text: The problem reveals cards in ascending order. Simulate the revealing procedure using index positions to discover where each sorted card belongs.

hints.title: Double-Ended Index Queue
hints.text: Initialize a double-ended container with indices 0 through n minus one. Pop the top index for the current card, then move the next available top index to the back.

hints.title: Ordered Card Placement
hints.text: Sort deck in ascending order. Prepare indices [0, 1, ..., n-1]. For each card in sorted deck: pop front index idx, assign ans[idx] = card. If indices remain, pop front index and append it to the back. Return ans.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from collections import deque

class Solution:
    def deckRevealedIncreasing(self, deck: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        deck.sort()
        n = len(deck)
        q = deque(range(n))
        res = [0] * n
        for card in deck:
            res[q.popleft()] = card
            if q:
                q.append(q.popleft())
        return res
```

variables: N: number of cards in deck
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Reversing card orders without tracking index positions requires complex trial-and-error permutations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Simulating the process forward on indices runs in O(N) steps following the initial O(N log N) sort.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should spot that simulating indices avoids messing with values until their exact target positions are determined.
complexity.notes: Double-ended queue operations take O(1) time each.
